title: With same app installed from distro and Flathub and pinned to Task Manager, Task Manager icons get confused about which one is running
line: When an app is installed both natively and as a Flatpak, each pinned launcher now shows its own windows.
explanation: Apps like Brave or Steam run under XWayland without naming their desktop file, so KWin looks for a desktop file whose StartupWMClass matches the window's WM_CLASS. The native and the Flatpak desktop files both match, and KWin always took the first one, so windows of both installs got the same desktop file and showed up under the same task manager launcher. When several desktop files match, KWin now reads the window process's systemd unit: windows in an app-flatpak-<id>-*.scope get the desktop file with that X-Flatpak id, the others get the non-Flatpak one.

commits.message:
x11window: pick the Flatpak or native desktop file the window runs from

When an app is installed both natively and as a Flatpak, both desktop
files share its StartupWMClass and the first one won for every window.
Now the window's systemd unit decides which of the two it belongs to.

BUG: 498875

media.caption: Before: both the native and the Flatpak window are grouped under the native launcher
Before: the Flatpak launcher (gamepad) stays inactive while its window is open
After: the native launcher only holds the native window
After: the Flatpak window shows under the Flatpak launcher, with its own icon

reviews.text: Using the window's systemd user unit via sd_pid_get_user_unit(pid()) in KWin (where X11Window::pid() comes from XResQueryClientIds and returns the host PID) is a sensible direction for disambiguating native vs Flatpak desktop files. However, the current patch has several concrete gaps: it does not account for systemd unit-name escaping of hyphens in Flatpak app IDs, it still only matches StartupWMClass against resourceName() (so comment 3's Steam case with WM_CLASS 'steamwebhelper'/'steam' and StartupWMClass=steam still fails to match in KWin), it only covers X11Window and not native Wayland apps that send an unprefixed app_id, and it introduces an unused-parameter warning on non-systemd builds.
changes: Handle systemd unit-name escaping when matching X-Flatpak against app-flatpak-<escaped_id>-*.scope (e.g., '-' in Flatpak IDs like org.DolphinEmu.dolphin-emu or io.gitlab.librewolf-community is escaped as \x2d in the systemd scope name).

Match StartupWMClass against resourceClass() as well as resourceName() (per the Desktop Entry Specification) so XWayland apps like Steam (comment 3, WM_CLASS = 'steamwebhelper', 'steam' with StartupWMClass=steam) actually enter the disambiguation path instead of returning zero matches.

Check and handle native Wayland windows (XdgToplevelWindow / shared Window logic) when a Flatpak Wayland app sends an unprefixed app_id matching a native desktop file, or clearly verify whether KWin/libtaskmanager resolves that case.
Silence the unused 'pid' parameter warning in systemdUserUnit(pid_t pid) when HAVE_SYSTEMD is 0 (e.g., Q_UNUSED(pid) or [[maybe_unused]]) so non-systemd builds such as FreeBSD stay warning-free.
